title: Tiered slab allocator with probabilistic eviction hints for KV cache fragmentation mitigation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Our KV cache experiences fragmentation that increases GPU memory pressure and eviction churn for workloads with a wide distribution of sequence lengths and variable token lifetimes. Continuous batching exacerbates this: batches mix short-lived small-prefix requests and long-lived long-sequence requests, causing allocation tail fragmentation and a rise in per-GPU working set overhead. Existing slab allocators and generational compaction approaches partially help but either increase latency during compaction or require global stop-the-world passes that violate latency SLOs.

Proposal summary: Implement a Tiered Slab Allocator combined with Probabilistic Eviction Hints and budgeted micro-compaction. The allocator splits the KV address space into a small-entry slab pool, a medium-entry slab pool, and a large-pool (chunked arena). Entries are classified on allocation by length and a short runtime lifetime prediction. The novelty: a lightweight probabilistic hint generator emits eviction/migration probabilities per entry that guide a background rebalancer to relocate high-probability-to-stay items into contiguous 'hot' slabs and push low-probability-to-stay items into reclaimable pools. Micro-compaction runs incrementally and is rate-limited by token throughput and latency budgets to avoid affecting tail latency. The design is continuous-batching aware: during high batching concurrency, relocation bandwidth is throttled and performed in small windows between minibatches; when batching is low, it opportunistically performs larger merges.

Key goals: reduce fragmentation ratio (free segments vs total) by >40% in mixed workloads, lower eviction churn (eviction events/sec) by >30%, reduce frequency of OOMs and allocation failures, and keep P50/P95 generation latency regression under 5%/10% respectively.

Technical components: 1) Tiered slab pools: fixed-size slab sizes tuned to token-length quantiles (e.g., 32B, 128B, 512B pages) with a large-chunk arena for >512B entries. 2) Lightweight entry fingerprint and metadata stored in a compact side-table: access counters (saturating 8-bit), last-access epoch (16-bit), size-class tag, and probabilistic 'stay score' (6-bit). 3) Probabilistic hint generator: sampled at allocation and on periodic hot-access windows: uses exponential decay counters and workload features (sequence length, reuse frequency, serving-timeouts) to output a stay-probability p in [0,1] discretized to 64 levels. 4) Background rebalancer: per-GPU thread that picks relocation candidates by combined score = stay_score * density_penalty and attempts to move them into contiguous slabs using GPU-to-GPU device memcpy or pinned-host staging when cross-GPU compaction is required. 5) Budgeted micro-compaction: relocation budget in bytes/sec and relocations/minute per GPU; budgets adjusted dynamically based on throughput SLOs, observed P95 latency, and active batch size. 6) Continuous-batching integration: relocation windows aligned to minibatch gaps, with a flag to temporarily pin entries actively referenced by in-flight batches. 7) GPU-friendly defrag kernels: scatter-gather copy kernels that coalesce dozens of small copies into batched vector copies to reduce kernel launches and PCIe overhead. 8) Fast-fallback policy: when compaction cannot keep up, promote a lightweight eviction policy to evict low stay-score entries first and emit a telemetry event for operator tuning.

Why this differs from prior work: rather than full generational compaction or heavy-handed defrag passes, this approach blends probabilistic predictions with tiered allocation and incremental, budgeted relocation that respects latency SLOs and batching behavior. The probabilistic hints drive smarter migration decisions (not simply LRU) and avoid unnecessary copies of cold items that briefly spike.

Metrics and telemetry to capture: fragmentation_ratio (free_bytes/total_bytes), eviction_churn/sec, relocations/sec, relocation_bytes/sec, in-flight_pin_rate, P50/P95/P99 latency of generation, batch_throughput tokens/sec, OOM_count, compaction_cpu_gpu_time, extra_pcie_bw_used, and stay_score distribution histograms. Add per-tenant and per-model breakdowns for observability.

Acceptance criteria (see below) and rollout plan included.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation ratio drop >= 40% in mixed seq-length synthetic workload compared to baseline allocator within 3 test runs
Eviction churn decreases by >= 30% on replay traces from 3 customers with mixed workloads
No increase in P50 generation latency > 5% and P95 latency > 10% during canary under production-like load
Relocation budget mechanism prevents visible tail latency regressions during stress tests (fail-open to conservative eviction)
Feature gated behind runtime-1.22 flag; full behavior disabled by default for existing Dedicated customers unless opt-in
End-to-end benchmarks and a reproducible synthetic harness are checked into infra/kvs/bench with PR and CI benchmarks attached
tasks: Design spec and microbenchmark plan (owner: Liam)
Side-table compact metadata layout and memory cost analysis
Implement tiered slab allocator prototype in runtime/algo/kv_slab.cc
Implement probabilistic hint generator and API hooks into allocation path
Develop background rebalancer and rate-limiter with continuous-batching awareness
GPU defrag kernel: scatter-gather batched copy + pinned staging implementation
Integrate with telemetry and expose metrics in Console (per-GPU and per-model)
Unit tests + stress tests (OOM/fenced scenarios) + performance harness
Run customer trace replays and collect comparative metrics vs baseline
Canary rollout to runtime-1.22 canary pool, monitor 72h, iterate on thresholds
design_notes: Choose slab size quantiles based on 95/75/50 token-length histograms from recent production traces
Keep side-table compact: target <1.5% additional RAM overhead relative to current KV metadata
Stay_score computed with lightweight EMA (alpha=0.3) on 8-bit counter; discretize to 64 buckets to fit in 6 bits
Relocation should avoid pinning entries referenced by in-flight minibatches; maintain a per-batch pin count with atomic ops
Budgeting strategy: soft budget (reduce relocation rate) and hard budget (stop relocation + trigger conservative eviction policy)
GPU defrag kernel must amortize PCIe overhead by aggregating small moves into >256KB batched transfers where possible
Fallbacks: when relocation stalls due to memory pressure, mark victim slabs as 'quarantine' for fast eviction
Expose tuning knobs: relocation_bytes_per_second, min_hot_run_length, quarantine_age_seconds, stay_score_threshold
Consider future: extend probabilistic model to include model-specific reuse patterns and token-position-aware features
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Relocation can increase P95 if not throttled. Mitigation: enforce hard budget and fail-open to eviction; run offline sims to tune budgets before canary.
Risk: Side-table overhead grows with number of entries. Mitigation: compact metadata fields, use relative epoch encodings, and evict long-tail cold entries earlier.
Risk: Cross-GPU compaction adds PCIe bandwidth pressure. Mitigation: prefer local-GPU rebalancing first; when necessary, schedule cross-GPU during low traffic windows and aggregate transfers.
Risk: Prediction errors cause unnecessary moves. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, hold-out validation, and enable per-tenant opt-outs.
Risk: Implementation complexity increases maintenance surface. Mitigation: modular design, feature flag for rapid rollback, and comprehensive unit tests
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Lab): implement prototype + unit tests; run microbenchmarks (2 engineers, 2 weeks)
Phase 1 (Bench): run large-scale replay on CI infra, tune budgets and thresholds (1 week)
Phase 2 (Canary): enable on small canary fleet with runtime-1.22 flag; monitor metrics for 72h; roll back on any P95 regressions or spike in eviction_churn (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (Ramp): gradually increase percent of traffic if canary stable; expose knobs in Console for ops teams; collect customer feedback (2-4 weeks)
Phase 4 (GA): enable by default for new deployments; provide migration guide for Dedicated customers and optional opt-in for legacy fleets
